## Re-diagnosis — the fix was applied and the incident has not cleared

A root cause was diagnosed, Planning built a fix for it, and Execution applied it
cleanly. Verify then re-checked the system end to end and the incident is still
present.

This is evidence, not a verdict on the prior diagnosis. Exactly one of the following
is true, and working out which one is the task:

- **The cause was right and the fix was insufficient.** The change addressed the cause
  only partially, or a second deviation on the same object or the same request path is
  still in place. If this is the case, name precisely what remains — do not reach for a
  different cause to explain evidence the prior one already explains.
- **The cause was a real fault, but not this incident's.** Something genuinely broken
  was found and repaired, yet it never explained the intake symptom. Two checks settle
  this: does the condition named predate the incident, and can it mechanically reach
  the symptom that is still being reported?
- **The cause was wrong.** The evidence gathered supports a different origin, and the
  fix changed something that was never on the failing path.

Run the specific checks that separate those three cases — a check that could come out
either way, not one that confirms what is already believed.
